landmarks.name: Rock Islands
landmarks.writeup: A group of limestone islands known for their unique mushroom-like shapes and rich marine biodiversity.

wiki.extract: The Rock Islands of Palau, also called Chelbacheb, are a collection of several hundred small limestone or coral uprises in the Southern Lagoon of Palau between Koror and Peleliu, now an incorporated part of Koror State. There are between 250 and 300 islands in the group according to different sources, with an aggregate area of 42 square kilometers (16 sq mi) and a maximum height of 207 meters (679 ft). The islands were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012.

landmarks.name: Jellyfish Lake
landmarks.writeup: A marine lake famous for its millions of harmless golden jellyfish, popular for snorkeling.

wiki.extract: Jellyfish Lake is a marine lake located on Eil Malk island in Palau. Eil Malk is a part of the Rock Islands, a group of small, rocky, mostly uninhabited islands in Palau's Southern Lagoon, between Koror and Peleliu. There are about 70 other marine lakes located throughout the Rock Islands. Millions of golden jellyfish migrate horizontally across the lake daily.

landmarks.name: Babeldaob Island
landmarks.writeup: The largest island in Palau, featuring lush forests, waterfalls, and ancient stone monoliths.

wiki.extract: Babeldaob is the largest island in the island nation of Palau. It is in the western Caroline Islands, and the second largest island in the Micronesia region of Oceania. Palau's capital, Ngerulmud, is located on Babeldaob, in Melekeok State.

cultural_events.name: Ngasech Traditional Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event celebrating Palauan culture with traditional dances, music, and crafts.

cultural_events.name: Palau Day
cultural_events.writeup: A national holiday commemorating Palau's independence with parades and cultural performances.

wiki.extract: Palau, officially the Republic of Palau, is an island country located in the Micronesia subregion of Oceania in the western Pacific Ocean. The Republic of Palau consists of approximately 340 islands and is the western part of the Caroline Islands, while the eastern and central parts make up the Federated States of Micronesia.

food_writeup: Palauan cuisine features seafood, taro, coconut, and tropical fruits, often prepared with traditional methods like grilling and boiling.
brief_history: Palau was settled around 3,000 years ago. It was colonized by Spain, Germany, and Japan before becoming a U.S. trust territory after World War II. Palau gained full sovereignty in 1994.

important_people.name: Thomas Remengesau Jr.
important_people.description: Former President and influential political leader

current_conflicts: Palau maintains peaceful relations internationally with no significant current conflicts.
